newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL STOCKS TUMBLE 3.32 PCT, MIRROR U.S. SLIDE.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL STOCKS TUMBLE 3.32 PCT, MIRROR U.S. SLIDE.

text.p: Brazilian stocks fell 3.32 percent in weak early afternoon trade, led by benchmark blue-chip Telebras, mirroring a slide in U.S. shares, brokers said.
"It's basically overseas markets causing this. There's no big local news," said a trader at local Sintese brokerage.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index .BVSP of 47 most- traded shares dropped 427 points to 12,445 points by 1300 local/1200 edt/1600 gmt on low turnover of 377.9 million reais ($349 million).
Brokers admitted they were puzzled by the steep decline, but said local shares extended early losses following drops on Wall Street in reaction to rising interest rates in the United States.
They said some investors, concerned by the early slide, may have begun taking profits on Brazilian stocks, which at the open were up more than 82 percent for the year.
Telebras preferred was hit especially hard, dropping 4.6 percent to 153.60 reais.
"With a stock that's risen 100 percent in six months, there's room for profit-taking," said John Carioba of Indusval brokerage.
Brokers also said speculation about a larger-than-expected trade deficit for July pushed stocks down in morning trade after trade figures were leaked to the market.
They cited a possible gap last month of up to $810 million reais. Economists had projected a $570 million July deficit.
Some traders also cited disappointment with Telebras half- year net profit of 1.5 billion reais, but others said the figures were in line with projections.
